newsitem.title: USA: Investors slowed mutual fund investments last month.
newsitem.headline: Investors slowed mutual fund investments last month.

text.p: Investors continued to put money into mutual funds that invest in stocks last month, though at the slowest rate in eight months.

The Investment Company Institute said Thursday the amount of cash invested in mutual funds that buy stocks fell in March to $9.5 billion, down from $18.45 billion in February. It was the smallest rate of investment since July, when investors put $5.75 billion into such mutual funds.

"You're not seeing what everybody has feared, and that is a wholesale bailing by mutual fund investors despite some very, very choppy market activity," said Tracey Gordon, a spokeswoman for Charles Schwab & Co.

Steven Norwitz, a spokesman for fund company T. Rowe Price Associates, said investors appeared unfazed by the 10 percent market correction in the days following the Federal Reserve's March 25 increase in interest rates.
"We have actually seen some money flow into the technology funds in the last few days," he said. "People did not panic in the midst of the correction."

Earlier this year, Vanguard Group and other fund companies had cautioned investors, many of whom had never experienced a major correction or a bear market, about the possibility of a downturn in stocks.
"Investors seemed to handle (the correction) with a greater sense of grace than many would have anticipated," Vanguard spokesman Brian Mattes said.
Charles Schwab, which sells more than 2,000 mutual funds from a wide variety of companies, saw investors move $4.5 million into aggressive growth funds so far in April, Gordon said.
In March, aggressive growth funds sold through Schwab lost about $209 million in sales as the market marched to record highs, she said.

Investors continued to seek a foreign shelter from the U.S. market volatility by buying international funds in early April, she said. The more conservative balanced funds, which invest stocks and bonds, became more popular in recent weeks after more than a year of being out of favour, she said.
Net sales of stock mutual funds offered by Schwab totalled $168 million in the first part of this month, with $33.6 million going towards balanced funds and $91 million going into index funds.
Vanguard Group, whose flagship $34 billion Index 500 Portfolio has benefitted from the growing popularity of index funds, also has seen investment sentiments shift within the last week.
"We're seeing individuals move back into equities again in the last day or two," Mattes said. "Investors are moving more eagerly towards equities now then they had in the prior two weeks."
ICI said bond and income funds had an estimated outflow of $1 billion in March, compared with an inflow of $2.17 billion in February.
